evidence.note: Forcignanò and Martinelli Tempesta place Hercher 31 among the extra-canonical Platonic epistles and discuss this material separately from the established thirteen-letter collection.
Hirsch (2026) explicitly enumerates Hercher 14, 15, 24, 25, 26, 30, 31, 70 and 85 as other letters of 'Plato' outside the thirteen-letter collection, pointing to the 2023 corpus-history treatment.
Natoli (2004) argues that the Thirty-first Socratic Letter is likely to be a genuine work of Plato and uses it as evidence for Plato's involvement in Macedonian affairs.

rationale: The letter to Philip is probably inauthentic on balance, but Anthony Natoli published a substantial defense of its Platonic authorship; this prevents a D classification.
